title: Cerulean watch — transition notes and temp runbook
content:
Quick context:
- Cerulean shift (11:00pm-7:00am PST) handoff notes.
- This is a working scratchpad: not polished, contains my mental checklist + temporary procedures to use until we land the formal runbook change in ops-config PR #188.

Summary of last 12h:
- 22:40: transient websocket saturation observed on hosted-api-01 in us-west-2. Error rates peaked (~3% 5xx) for 6m before automatic routing fallback to hosted-api-02 kicked in.
- 23:05: cache eviction storms on redis-cache-prod-2 correlated with increased model-serving cold starts (kv-cache misses). Suspect a mis-sized eviction policy after the job that trimmed prefix cache earlier today.
- 01:10: Incident follow-up created (OPS-342). Short-term mitigations applied: increased redis maxmemory-policy to volatile-lru on prod pool, bumped instance counts for hosted-api-02 by +1 replica to recover capacity.
- No customer SLA violations (all within retries/fallbacks), but need a cleaner permanent fix and a debrief.

What to watch for on this shift:
- sustained increase in websocket 5xx (>1% over 15m) on any hosted api node
- redis eviction bursts: look for 'evicted_keys' spikes > 5000/min on prod clusters
- model cold-start latency > 800ms P95 for repeated requests to the same session (indicates KV cache flushing)

Quick checks (copy/paste):
- Tail API error logs: kubectl -n hosted-api logs -l app=hosted-api -f --since=15m | grep "5.."
- Check websocket connections: redis-cli -h redis-proxy-1 info clients | grep connected_clients
- Eviction metrics: curl -s http://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query?query=increase(redis_evicted_keys_total[1m]) | jq .data.result
- Model KV cache size: redwoodctl cache status --model=rw-v1 --pod hosted-api-01

Temporary runbook snippet (use these steps while PR #188 is reviewed):
1) If websocket 5xx > 1% sustained for 15m:
   - Add replica to fallback pool: redwoodctl scale --deployment=hosted-api-02 --add 1
   - Route new traffic away from affected node in Console: Console > Routing > Node policies > mark hosted-api-01 as draining
   - Post slack update in #infra-oncall with incident tag and brief summary.

2) If redis eviction bursts detected:
   - Switch policy temporarily to volatile-lru on the affected pool: redis-cli -h redis-admin CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy volatile-lru
   - If evicted_keys remains high after 5m, promote read-heavy caches to cache-shard-03 (maintenance window permitting).
   - Create a short ticket to revert later and annotate OPS-342.

3) If model cold starts observed:
   - Warm the KV cache for the popular model variants: redwoodctl warm --model=rw-v1 --prefixes-file=/tmp/top-prefixes.txt --parallel=4
   - If warming fails due to memory, reduce parallelism and run again.

Escalation contacts (order):
- On-call SRE (primary): Ravi Menon — pager: @ravi.ops — slack: @ravi
- Senior infra (secondary): Elena Garcia — email: elena@redwood.ai — pager: @elena.ops
- Platform eng lead (tertiary): Tomas Leclerc — slack: @tomas

Notes to self / things to follow up:
- Confirm why the prefix-trimming job ran at ~22:35 (linked PR or cron?). I saw a manual trigger in ops-config history but couldn't find the author. Action: add a note to OPS-342 to trace back commit ID.
- Ask product infra team if recent model rollout (rw-v1.3) changed KV cache keys (could explain spike in misses).
- Add a synthetic check for KV cache miss rate to the hosted-api SLOs (short-term alert: KV miss rate > 10% for 10m).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Was the websocket saturation triggered by a client-side retry loop (we saw repeated identical session ids)? Needs app team confirmation.
- Are there any scheduled batch jobs hitting prefix cache at midnight? If yes, mitigate via rate-limits.

Immediate TODOs for incoming shift (if you are the handoff receiver):
- Verify OPS-342 status and attach any fresh logs to the ticket.
- Run the "Quick checks" above and paste outputs to the ticket.
- If you change redis policy, annotate the change in the ticket and set a reminder to revert after root cause is addressed.
- Ping Ravi if you need to scale replicas quickly — he's awake for next 2 hours.

Log snippets to keep (paste to ticket if needed):
- sample: "2024-11-02T22:41:12Z hosted-api-01 websocket error: upstream reset code=502 session=abc123"
- sample: "2024-11-02T22:58:03Z redis-cache-prod-2 evicted_keys=8732 used_memory=1.9GB maxmemory=2.0GB"

Final: This is a short-term, messy doc. I'll clean and propose a permanent runbook in Confluence next week. For now, follow the temporary steps and escalate if anything looks like degradation >30m or customer-facing errors start to appear.

— Maya

(previous shifts: see attached quicknotes in drive; I will link more after morning)
